addenda.title: The rooms, the plumbing walls and the service annex
items: 1. Every room as a space (IfcSpace), 122 in all: its use, the openings in its walls and its net floor area, from forge `rooms` (pass 3g step 1).

5. Each bedroom's escape window named (24): its own type (W3), side-hinged (a casement), since hung or sliding a window of their size can't clear IBC 2021 1031; every window now says whether it is one (Pset_WindowCommon.FireExit).

addenda.title: The envelope to Pennsylvania's 2021 energy code
items: Item 1 (walls): the exterior walls, and the service annex's, take R-3.8 continuous insulation (1 in. of board outboard of the sheathing) over the R-20 cavities: U-0.051, the 2021 IECC's (Table R402.1.3, 20 + 3.8). The walls thicken inward from 7 to 8 in.; the building's outside stays 100 x 40 ft, so the rooms along the outside walls lose 1 in. and the stair, set against the back wall, moves with it.
Item 2 (slabs): the ground floor's heated slab sits on R-5 under its full area, with R-10 at its edge to 4 ft; the annex's slab takes the same edge insulation (Table R402.1.3 and its footnote d).
The windows (U-0.30) and the roof (R-49) already meet the 2021 code: no change.

addenda.title: The glass: ENERGY STAR's Northern zone, at a solar heat gain that sizes the cooling
items: Item 1 (glass): every window and patio door is rated, whole unit, at a U-factor of at most 0.22 Btu/h ft2 F (NFRC 100; the code asks 0.30), a solar heat gain coefficient from 0.17 to 0.25 (NFRC 200) and air leakage of at most 0.3 cfm/ft2: ENERGY STAR v7's Northern zone, which all of western Pennsylvania is in. The window and door schedule now carries the U-factor and the SHGC (Pset_DoorWindowGlazingType.SolarHeatGainTransmittance).

Why: the flats' cooling (step 3c). The schedule gave no SHGC, and the cooling design had assumed 0.35: at that, no 1-ton unit covers a flat; at this glass one does. The winter sun the glass gives up is heat the data center's loop supplies anyway.
Why the U-factor: ENERGY STAR, chosen beyond the code; it lowers the flats' heat, and the water their floors need.
No drawing changes; no opening moves or resizes.

addenda.title: The services, the frame, the stair's enclosure and the roof hatch
items: Item 1 (the stair's enclosure and the annex, IBC 2021 1023.7 and 1023.2): the annex's walls annex-left, annex-right, within 10 ft of the stair's unrated back windows above the annex, are rated 1 hour from the ground to the annex's roof, over their whole length; the door annex-mechanical/left/0 is a 45-minute fire door assembly, self-closing and latching; and the stair's back wall where the annex meets it (the wall between the stair walls, ext-back-1-stair) is part of the stair's 1-hour enclosure.

Item 2 (the roof hatch, IMC 2021 306.5 and IBC 2021 1011.16): a 30 x 36 in. insulated roof hatch over the stair's top hall, 10.5 ft from the roof's edge (no guards: 1011.13), and a fixed steel ladder to it against the hall's side wall, 18 in. between its rails, its rungs at most 14 in. apart and its rails 30 in. above the roof; the hall keeps 73 in. clear beside it. The hatch is an opaque door in the envelope, at most U-0.20.

Item 3 (the frame): the completed wood frame is issued, framing-addendum-5.ifc: the flats' partitions and plumbing walls, the service annex, the stair halls' floors and the roof hatch's opening (doubled trimmers and headers), with the shell's members. It replaces Addendum 3's frame, which was for reference.

Item 4 (the services): the services model is issued, services-addendum-5.ifc, 3,118 elements in their systems: heating, cooling and air 2,678 ft; plumbing 4,008 ft; sprinklers 1,319 ft; wiring 6,567 ft of pipe, duct, conduit and cable, with their fittings, fixtures, equipment and sprinklers. Its schedules: lengths, fittings, equipment, fixtures, sprinklers, registers, switches, holes through the frame and the firestop schedule. For the trades:
a. PEX is bent on a bend support at its turns; elbows only at the fixtures' stub-outs, the risers' feet, where the top flat's branch leaves its riser and at the manifolds.
b. Holes through studs, plates and joists are bored at the member's centre: there every pipe and cable clears NEC 300.4(A)(1), IPC 305.6, IMC 305.5 and NFPA 13R 5.2.3.7 without a steel plate.
c. The feeders' PVC conduit runs straight under the slab between its stub-ups, at most 356° of bends from the meter to a panel (NEC 352.26: 360°), with no pull point between.
d. A 2 in. vent stack in each column's plumbing wall (IPC 905.1, Table 906.1).
e. Each mini-split's static pressure is set to its ducts by Fujitsu's function setting, and each takes a UL 508 water-level switch at its drain, wired to its forced stop (IMC 307.2.3 item 4).

Item 5 (firestopping, IBC 2021 714): 453 openings through rated assemblies, each by its condition in the firestop schedule. Listed systems where they fit as tested (STI F-C-1074, STI F-C-2032); for the other 345, the same maker's engineering judgments, submitted for the authority's approval. Pipe insulation stops at each face of a rated floor (714.3); partitions under a rated ceiling are sheathed in Type X gypsum board and the ceiling is tight to their double top plates (714.5.2 exception 7); the top storey's ceiling, a roof/ceiling Type V-B doesn't rate, and the stair's halls take fireblocking only (718.2.1.4). Every listed floor system found is tested in UL L500 floors; the walk-up's is AWC's WIJ-1.3 (Item 6), so each takes the authority's acceptance or the maker's engineering judgment for it.

Item 6 (the floors between flats, IBC 2021 711.2.4.3): 1-hour, built as AWC DCA 3 (Feb 2024) WIJ-1.3: 23/32 in. tongue-and-groove sheathing glued and nailed to the I-joists, 2 in. of 3.5 pcf mineral wool batts on 1x4 setting strips along the bottom flanges, resilient channels 16 in. o.c., and one layer of 5/8 in. Type C gypsum board screwed 7 in. o.c. It replaces WIJ-1.1, which the bid set named: WIJ-1.1 asks I-joist flanges of 5.25 in.2 and the PRI-60's are 1-1/2 x 2-5/16 in. (3.5 in.2); WIJ-1.3 asks 2.25. No UL L500 design matches the floor (the I-joist ones name one maker's joists, and two layers of board under resilient channels). Sound (AWC's TR15 estimates, joists 16 in. o.c., 1 in. of gypsum concrete): STC 57; IIC 59 under carpet and pad but 46 under cushioned vinyl, short of IBC 1206.3's 50: a hard floor finish needs a tested underlayment, chosen with the interiors.

addenda.title: The fire service's control valves, the house panel and the services drawn
items: Item 1 (the fire service's control valves, NFPA 13R 2019 and IBC 2021 903.4): a listed indicating shutoff valve on each side of the 2 in. double check valve assembly, OS&Y gate valves as the basis of design, each supervised by a tamper switch to the monitoring panel. Watts lists its 2 in. LF007 as 'UL Classified without shutoff valves only', so the assembly's own valves can't serve as the system's control valves, as step 6 had them. The hydraulics count the two (NFPA 13's chart: a 2 in. gate valve is 1 ft of Schedule 40 steel pipe): 0.06 psi at the most demanding design (3-front-left's open area, 56 gpm), which now needs 44.8 of the 45 psi the street gives less its margin; 0.30 psi of 36.4 at the stair's 6 sprinklers. A butterfly valve is 6 ft on the same chart and would make it 45.1 psi, over what the street gives: an equal loses no more than a gate valve.

Item 2 (the house panel, NEC 2020 Article 220 and 215.2(A)(1)): the swing tank's element is 2.0 kW (Bradford White's RE340S6 takes 1.5 to 6 kW elements; the 1.75 kW the hot-water plant was sized at isn't made), and it is a continuous load: the design day's heat from it takes 4.9 h at 2.0 kW, in the quiet hours. The house loads come to 10,291 VA calculated, 47.3 A a leg: the house feeder, its breaker and its position on the meter stack are 50 A (step 5 had 45 A, on 1.75 kW counted noncontinuous). The house panel's 120% rule now takes 16.6 kW AC of the roof's PV.

Item 3 (the services drawn): the services set as 21 sheets, services-sheets-addendum-6.pdf: the index and general notes (G-001); each trade's plan of each storey and the roof, every run tagged with its system and size; the four plumbing walls in elevation, every trade in them over the frame; the water service and the hot-water plant, the heating loop and the flats' air, the one-line and the panel schedules, the fire service and its hydraulic summary. Drawn from the bid set's models and the designs on the routes, they add nothing to the models.

addenda.title: Each flat's hot-water loop, the plant's storage and backup heater, the control sequence and the tests
items: Item 1 (the hot water, IECC 2021 C404): a plant serving several flats comes under the energy code's commercial hot-water rules (R403.8), which the bid set's hot water didn't meet. Each flat's hot water is now a loop of its own: its hot branch runs past its fixtures to its lavatory, where a thermostatic balancing valve in the vanity starts its 0.5 in. return to the return riser: Caleffi ThermoSetter 116, 1/2 in. (basis of design), set 124 F, reached through the vanity's doors (C404.6: with access). Each fixture's own pipe is sized for it (tub 0.75, lav 0.5, sink 0.75, dishwasher 0.75, washer 0.75 in.): no fixture holds more than 64 fl oz from the loop (C404.5.2; the worst 53, 1-back-left's tub). The flats' hot pipe and returns are insulated 1 in. (C404.4, Table C403.12.3), stopped at each plate and joist, their holes bored for the bare pipe. P-3 runs while the return at the swing tank is under 122 F and stops at 124 F (C404.6.1); it moves 4.79 gpm at 3.3 ft round the longest circuit, within its rated 10.7 gpm at 8.202 ft. The returns: 1.25 in. main, 0.75 in. risers. The loop loses 176 W a flat (72 in the risers and mains).

Item 2 (the hot-water plant): with each flat's loop, Ecosizer asks 255 gal of storage on the routes (259 on the square lengths), over the 250 gal tank Addendum 5's model placed. The storage is now 2 Lochinvar HP150G tanks in series, 300 gal (basis of design): cold in at ST-1B's bottom, hot out of ST-1A's top, for stratification. The next single tank, 450 gal and 49 in. across, wouldn't pass the mechanical room's 42 in. door. The swing tank's element is 4.5 kW (Ecosizer asks 4.03 kW on the square lengths, 3.70 on the routes; Bradford White makes 4.0 and 4.5 at 208 V); the plant's capacity 11.63 kW. The mechanical room's floor: the tanks along its far wall, the heat pump by the door, the swing tank and the backup heater (Item 3) on the back wall, each with its maker's service space; the plant's mains drop through the slab 12 in. off the wall to the building.

Item 3 (when the data center's heat is gone): a backup heater, BK-1, on the heater circuit after HP-1: A. O. Smith DRE-52-12 (basis of design), 12.3 kW against the plant's 11.63, its elements locked out unless the data center's water is gone, and never energized with HP-1 enabled (its contactor's coil wired through a normally closed contact of HP-1's enable). The flats are heated by their mini-splits alone: each covers its flat at the design temperature (-16.3 C), the least margin 1-back-left's 4,080 W against 1,986. The wiring counts each flat's heating as its heat pump and the ERV's preheater together: each feeder at most 91.0 A on its 100 A breaker; the house panel 110 A (108.4 A calculated: BK-1 counted, HP-1 not, NEC 220.60); the service 463 A on its 600 A main. The house panel's 120% rule now takes 6.7 kW AC of the roof's PV.

Item 4 (the building loop's pump): P-1, Grundfos ALPHA2 15-55F (basis of design), needs 10.7 ft at 6.04 gpm on its worst path (1-front-left), against 12.3 ft on its curve III, its highest fixed speed, with 10% kept in hand; the loop's risers 0.75 in.

Item 5 (the control sequence): specification section 23 09 93 (spec-23-09-93-sequence.md) is issued, 31 steps in 5 systems, normal running and the fallback, 3 interlocks wired, not programmed, and 17 control points. 8 points are still to select by the bidder (PC-1, TS-1, FS-1, V-1, P-2, TS-5, V-2, TS-2).

Item 6 (the tests and inspections): specification section 01 45 00 (spec-01-45-00-tests.md) is issued, 28 items in 9 areas (plumbing, hot water, building loop, mini-splits, ventilation, envelope, fire protection, general, electrical): what, who, when and what passes, 24 of them the codes' own tests quoted in their words, the rest the design's claims to be proved at commissioning.

Item 7 (the services model and the sheets, reissued): services-addendum-7.ifc, 3,162 elements. Against Addendum 5's, 59 added (each flat's return and its balancing valve, the plant's two tanks and backup heater), 15 removed (the one storage tank, and fittings of runs routed again), 532 changed in route, length or size, most of them routed again around the flats' returns; by system: cold 0 added, 55 changed, 0 removed; hot 47 added, 234 changed, 5 removed; loop 0 added, 35 changed, 0 removed; power 0 added, 148 changed, 0 removed; vent 12 added, 60 changed, 10 removed. Its schedules are reissued with it. The services sheets, services-sheets-addendum-7.pdf: 23 sheets, G-002 (the tests) and M-602 (the sequence) new, P-601 and M-601 revised, every plan and elevation redrawn from the revised model. They replace Addendum 6's sheets.
